heroes.name: Warrior Priest
heroes.text:
Warrior Priest

Starting adjustment: Strength -1, Bravery +1.

Healing spells equal total Fate points (two for a beginning priest).

Holding a holy symbol in one hand can frighten Undead in the priest's death zone: at the start of their turn they must pass a Bravery roll, modified by the priest's total Fate, or be unable to act. The other hand may hold a one-handed weapon or shield.

Only crushing or bruising weapons; no blades.

Apply abilities manually during play.

heroes.name: Rogue
heroes.text:
Rogue

Starting adjustments: WS -1, Bravery -1, Speed +1, BS +1.

+1 to rolls for secret doors, treasure, spotting traps and surprise. With thieves' tools, add total Fate to disarm-trap rolls (initially +2).

Tools also allow locking/unlocking doors or chests and setting traps, rolling against current Speed.

No more than +1 from any single armour piece; shields allowed.

Apply abilities manually during play.

heroes.name: Fighter
heroes.text:
Fighter

Use the racial profile. If WS is below 7, add 1; if Strength is below 4, add 1. Deduct the same total from Intelligence and/or Speed.

Attack rerolls per expedition equal total Fate. Each rerolls one attack die just rolled.

Optional berserker: Intelligence -2, BS -2, WS -1 only if this would not take WS below 7. Record the choice in the hero's name and edit the stats; use the rulebook's berserker rules.

Any weapons and armour permitted. Apply abilities manually during play.

heroes.name: Mage
heroes.text:
Mage

Use the racial profile. If Intelligence is below 7, you may add up to 2, deducting the same total from Strength and/or WS. This preset uses a human suggestion with WS -1 and Intelligence +1.

Human and Elf mages start with their college's first four spells. Dwarf mages start with one chosen spell and pay double to learn new spells.

No armour; only daggers or a staff in combat.

Edit stats for your chosen race and apply spells manually during play.
